questions.question: A web page is mainly built from three technologies. (a) defines the structure of the page, (b) specifies its appearance, and (c) adds behavior and interactivity. Fill in the blanks (a)–(c).
HTML defines the structure or skeleton of a web page.
CSS specifies the appearance of a web page, including colors, layout, size, and fonts.
JavaScript adds behavior and interactivity to a web page.
CSS is responsible for adding interactive behavior to buttons and forms.
For each task, indicate which technology is used: A HTML, B CSS, C JavaScript.
items: c. Making a button respond to a click
f. Updating part of the screen

questions.question: Which statement most appropriately describes semantic HTML?
options: Using HTML element names that indicate the meaning of each part of the page
Using CSS to change the appearance of a page
questions.answer: Using HTML element names that indicate the meaning of each part of the page

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an appropriate benefit of semantic HTML?
options: Screen readers can better understand the structure of the page
Search engines can more easily understand the content
The display speed of a web page necessarily becomes faster
Information can be easier to convey to users with visual impairments
questions.answer: The display speed of a web page necessarily becomes faster

questions.question: What is accessibility?
questions.answer: The website being usable by people with impairments.

questions.question: What is SEO?
questions.answer: Helping search engines understand and find the content.

questions.question: What is responsive design?
questions.answer: A design concept in which the layout automatically adjusts according to different screen sizes such as PCs, smartphones, and tablets.

questions.question: What is the mobile-first approach?
questions.answer: Starting by prioritizing smaller screens such as smartphones when designing the page.

questions.question: Which of the following most appropriately describes a framework?
options: A language for defining the structure of a web page
A structure for making web application development more efficient
A technology for encrypting data and sending it safely
A design concept for supporting different screen sizes
questions.answer: A structure for making web application development more efficient

questions.question: Match each framework with its appropriate characteristic.
items: a. Developed by Meta and suited to large-scale web applications
b. Has a simple structure and supports incremental construction
c. Adds mechanisms to speed up page display in addition to React features

questions.question: Think as an Engineer — A student club wants a simple web page that lists its events, is styled in the club's colors, and has a button showing how many people have signed up. Which technology handles each feature: HTML, CSS, or JavaScript? Explain.
questions.answer: HTML handles the event list because it defines the page structure and content. CSS handles the club's colors and layout because it specifies appearance. JavaScript handles the live sign-up counter because it adds behavior and updates the page.

questions.question: Think as an Engineer — Name one change that would make the student club page easier to read on a phone, and one semantic-HTML choice that would help a screen reader.
questions.answer: Use responsive design so the layout adjusts to the phone's screen size. Use meaningful semantic elements such as header, nav, main, or footer so a screen reader can better understand the page structure.

questions.question: Think as an Engineer — Recommend whether the student club should separate HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and give two reasons.
questions.answer: Yes. HTML holds the content and structure, CSS controls the appearance, and JavaScript adds behavior. Separating their roles makes the page easier to understand, develop, and maintain.

questions.question: New Context — A news site must look good on phones and be found easily by search engines. Name one responsive-design choice and one semantic-HTML choice it should make, and say what each one improves.
questions.answer: Use a responsive layout that adjusts to different screen sizes to improve usability on phones. Use meaningful semantic elements such as header, nav, and main to improve accessibility and help search engines understand the content.

questions.question: Reflect & Challenge — Of structure, style, and behavior, which do you notice most when a web page is badly made, and why?
questions.answer: Any of the three can be noticeable. Poor structure can make information confusing, poor style can make the page difficult to read, and poor behavior can make buttons or other interactions fail.
